modules.title: Determine high-performing and/or scalable storage solutions

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: Amazon S3 provides __________, Amazon EBS provides block storage for compute, and Amazon EFS or Amazon FSx provide managed file systems.

reveal.text: Amazon S3 provides object storage, Amazon EBS provides block storage for compute, and Amazon EFS or Amazon FSx provide managed file systems.

prompts.label: ⏱️ WHEN?
prompts.placeholder: Choose storage by __________: object APIs for objects, low-latency block devices for instance storage, and shared file protocols for file workloads.

reveal.text: Choose storage by access semantics: object APIs for objects, low-latency block devices for instance storage, and shared file protocols for file workloads.

prompts.label: 🚫 NOT THIS
prompts.placeholder: Do not choose EBS as a general __________ or S3 when an application requires a mounted POSIX file system.

reveal.text: Do not choose EBS as a general multi-AZ shared file system or S3 when an application requires a mounted POSIX file system.

prompts.label: 🎯 EXAM CLUE
prompts.placeholder: Shared Linux file access across many instances points to __________; persistent block storage for one EC2 instance points to EBS.

reveal.text: Shared Linux file access across many instances points to EFS; persistent block storage for one EC2 instance points to EBS.

source_refs.title: Determine high-performing and/or scalable storage solutions — official exam guide
Object, block, and file storage — AWS documentation

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: EBS SSD volumes such as gp3 and io2 are optimized for __________, while st1 and sc1 HDD volumes target large sequential throughput workloads.

reveal.text: EBS SSD volumes such as gp3 and io2 are optimized for transactional IOPS, while st1 and sc1 HDD volumes target large sequential throughput workloads.

prompts.label: ⏱️ WHEN?
prompts.placeholder: Use __________ for general-purpose price/performance, io2 for demanding sustained IOPS, st1 for frequently accessed sequential throughput, and sc1 for colder sequential data.

reveal.text: Use gp3 for general-purpose price/performance, io2 for demanding sustained IOPS, st1 for frequently accessed sequential throughput, and sc1 for colder sequential data.

prompts.label: 🚫 NOT THIS
prompts.placeholder: Do not use st1 or sc1 as __________ or for small random I/O workloads that need high IOPS.

reveal.text: Do not use st1 or sc1 as boot volumes or for small random I/O workloads that need high IOPS.

prompts.label: 🎯 EXAM CLUE
prompts.placeholder: A database with demanding random I/O points to __________-backed EBS rather than throughput-oriented HDD.

reveal.text: A database with demanding random I/O points to SSD-backed EBS rather than throughput-oriented HDD.

source_refs.title: Determine high-performing and/or scalable storage solutions — official exam guide
EBS SSD and HDD performance — AWS documentation

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: AWS DataSync accelerates __________, Storage Gateway exposes hybrid storage interfaces, and Snow Family devices support large offline or edge data-transfer scenarios.

reveal.text: AWS DataSync accelerates online data movement, Storage Gateway exposes hybrid storage interfaces, and Snow Family devices support large offline or edge data-transfer scenarios.

prompts.label: ⏱️ WHEN?
prompts.placeholder: Choose among online transfer, hybrid local interfaces, and physical-device transfer based on __________, dataset size, ongoing access, and migration windows.

reveal.text: Choose among online transfer, hybrid local interfaces, and physical-device transfer based on bandwidth, dataset size, ongoing access, and migration windows.

prompts.label: 🚫 NOT THIS
prompts.placeholder: Do not use a physical Snow device for a __________ transfer when adequate network bandwidth and DataSync already meet the schedule.

reveal.text: Do not use a physical Snow device for a small recurring transfer when adequate network bandwidth and DataSync already meet the schedule.

prompts.label: 🎯 EXAM CLUE
prompts.placeholder: A repeated NFS-to-S3 transfer over the network points to __________; a local file interface backed by AWS storage points to Storage Gateway.

reveal.text: A repeated NFS-to-S3 transfer over the network points to DataSync; a local file interface backed by AWS storage points to Storage Gateway.

source_refs.title: Determine high-performing and/or scalable storage solutions — official exam guide
Hybrid storage and transfer — AWS documentation

modules.title: Design high-performing and elastic compute solutions

nodes.title: EC2 instance families and workload fit

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: EC2 instance families balance compute, memory, storage, networking, and accelerator resources for different __________.

reveal.text: EC2 instance families balance compute, memory, storage, networking, and accelerator resources for different workload profiles.

prompts.label: ⏱️ WHEN?
prompts.placeholder: Select __________ instances for CPU-bound work, memory-optimized instances for large in-memory datasets, and accelerated instances when GPUs or other accelerators are required.

reveal.text: Select compute-optimized instances for CPU-bound work, memory-optimized instances for large in-memory datasets, and accelerated instances when GPUs or other accelerators are required.

prompts.label: 🚫 NOT THIS
prompts.placeholder: Do not select instance size only from __________ when memory, network, storage, or accelerator needs are the actual bottleneck.

reveal.text: Do not select instance size only from vCPU count when memory, network, storage, or accelerator needs are the actual bottleneck.

prompts.label: 🎯 EXAM CLUE
prompts.placeholder: A CPU-bound batch workload points to a __________ family; a large in-memory cache points to memory optimized.

reveal.text: A CPU-bound batch workload points to a compute-optimized family; a large in-memory cache points to memory optimized.

source_refs.title: Design high-performing and elastic compute solutions — official exam guide
EC2 instance families and workload fit — AWS documentation

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: Lambda allocates CPU and other resources in proportion to __________, and concurrency controls how many function executions can run at the same time.

reveal.text: Lambda allocates CPU and other resources in proportion to configured memory, and concurrency controls how many function executions can run at the same time.

prompts.label: ⏱️ WHEN?
prompts.placeholder: Tune memory with __________ and use reserved or provisioned concurrency when the workload needs concurrency control or reduced cold-start latency.

reveal.text: Tune memory with performance measurements and use reserved or provisioned concurrency when the workload needs concurrency control or reduced cold-start latency.

prompts.label: 🚫 NOT THIS
prompts.placeholder: Do not assume the __________ memory size is cheapest when a slower function can increase billed duration.

reveal.text: Do not assume the smallest memory size is cheapest when a slower function can increase billed duration.

prompts.label: 🎯 EXAM CLUE
prompts.placeholder: If increasing Lambda __________ makes CPU-bound work finish much faster, total cost can stay similar or fall despite the higher per-millisecond rate.

reveal.text: If increasing Lambda memory makes CPU-bound work finish much faster, total cost can stay similar or fall despite the higher per-millisecond rate.

source_refs.title: Design high-performing and elastic compute solutions — official exam guide
Lambda memory, concurrency, and scaling — AWS documentation

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: AWS Batch manages __________, ECS and EKS orchestrate containers, Fargate runs containers without managing servers, and Lambda runs event-driven functions.

reveal.text: AWS Batch manages batch job scheduling, ECS and EKS orchestrate containers, Fargate runs containers without managing servers, and Lambda runs event-driven functions.

prompts.label: ⏱️ WHEN?
prompts.placeholder: Match the compute model to job __________, packaging, orchestration, control requirements, and operational overhead.

reveal.text: Match the compute model to job duration, packaging, orchestration, control requirements, and operational overhead.

prompts.label: 🚫 NOT THIS
prompts.placeholder: Do not force __________ container workloads into Lambda when container orchestration or Batch better matches execution requirements.

reveal.text: Do not force long-running container workloads into Lambda when container orchestration or Batch better matches execution requirements.

prompts.label: 🎯 EXAM CLUE
prompts.placeholder: Queued large-scale batch jobs with variable compute demand point to __________.

reveal.text: Queued large-scale batch jobs with variable compute demand point to AWS Batch.

source_refs.title: Design high-performing and elastic compute solutions — official exam guide
Batch, containers, and serverless compute — AWS documentation

nodes.title: Relational, key-value, graph, document, and warehouse databases

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: AWS provides __________ databases such as RDS and Aurora for relational workloads, DynamoDB for key-value and document access, Neptune for graph relationships, and Redshift for analytics warehousing.

reveal.text: AWS provides purpose-built databases such as RDS and Aurora for relational workloads, DynamoDB for key-value and document access, Neptune for graph relationships, and Redshift for analytics warehousing.

prompts.label: ⏱️ WHEN?
prompts.placeholder: Choose the database model from __________, consistency, query shape, scale, and operational requirements rather than selecting one engine for every workload.

reveal.text: Choose the database model from access patterns, consistency, query shape, scale, and operational requirements rather than selecting one engine for every workload.

prompts.label: 🚫 NOT THIS
prompts.placeholder: Do not choose a __________ solely because data is structured when the workload is a massive predictable key-value access pattern.

reveal.text: Do not choose a relational database solely because data is structured when the workload is a massive predictable key-value access pattern.

prompts.label: 🎯 EXAM CLUE
prompts.placeholder: Known partition-key access at very large scale points to __________; complex joins and transactions often point to a relational engine.

reveal.text: Known partition-key access at very large scale points to DynamoDB; complex joins and transactions often point to a relational engine.

source_refs.title: Determine high-performing database solutions — official exam guide
Relational, key-value, graph, document, and warehouse databases — AWS documentation

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: Amazon ElastiCache provides general in-memory caching, while DynamoDB Accelerator is a __________ cache designed for microsecond read access to DynamoDB data.

reveal.text: Amazon ElastiCache provides general in-memory caching, while DynamoDB Accelerator is a DynamoDB-compatible cache designed for microsecond read access to DynamoDB data.

prompts.label: ⏱️ WHEN?
prompts.placeholder: Use DAX for __________ DynamoDB workloads that benefit from API-compatible caching, and ElastiCache for broader caching, session, or in-memory data-structure needs.

reveal.text: Use DAX for read-heavy DynamoDB workloads that benefit from API-compatible caching, and ElastiCache for broader caching, session, or in-memory data-structure needs.

prompts.label: 🚫 NOT THIS
prompts.placeholder: Do not use DAX as a cache in front of __________ because DAX is designed specifically for DynamoDB.

reveal.text: Do not use DAX as a cache in front of RDS because DAX is designed specifically for DynamoDB.

prompts.label: 🎯 EXAM CLUE
prompts.placeholder: Microsecond reads with minimal application change to a DynamoDB workload point to __________.

reveal.text: Microsecond reads with minimal application change to a DynamoDB workload point to DAX.

source_refs.title: Determine high-performing database solutions — official exam guide
ElastiCache and DAX — AWS documentation

nodes.title: Read replicas, Aurora readers, and RDS Proxy

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: Read replicas and Aurora reader instances __________, while RDS Proxy primarily improves connection management and reuse.

reveal.text: Read replicas and Aurora reader instances scale read traffic, while RDS Proxy primarily improves connection management and reuse.

prompts.label: ⏱️ WHEN?
prompts.placeholder: Use readers for read throughput and RDS Proxy when __________ from serverless or microservice clients is the main database pressure.

reveal.text: Use readers for read throughput and RDS Proxy when connection churn from serverless or microservice clients is the main database pressure.

prompts.label: 🚫 NOT THIS
prompts.placeholder: Do not add RDS Proxy expecting it to create additional __________ or increase the database's storage capacity.

reveal.text: Do not add RDS Proxy expecting it to create additional read replicas or increase the database's storage capacity.

prompts.label: 🎯 EXAM CLUE
prompts.placeholder: Read-heavy SQL traffic points to __________; too many short-lived connections points to RDS Proxy.

reveal.text: Read-heavy SQL traffic points to replicas; too many short-lived connections points to RDS Proxy.

source_refs.title: Determine high-performing database solutions — official exam guide
Read replicas, Aurora readers, and RDS Proxy — AWS documentation

modules.title: Determine high-performing and/or scalable network architectures

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: CloudFront is a content delivery network that __________ and delivers HTTP content from edge locations, while Global Accelerator uses the AWS global network to improve availability and performance for TCP and UDP applications.

reveal.text: CloudFront is a content delivery network that caches and delivers HTTP content from edge locations, while Global Accelerator uses the AWS global network to improve availability and performance for TCP and UDP applications.

prompts.label: ⏱️ WHEN?
prompts.placeholder: Use CloudFront for cacheable web content and Global Accelerator when global clients need static __________ and optimized network paths to regional endpoints.

reveal.text: Use CloudFront for cacheable web content and Global Accelerator when global clients need static anycast IPs and optimized network paths to regional endpoints.

prompts.label: 🚫 NOT THIS
prompts.placeholder: Do not choose Global Accelerator when the core requirement is __________ of objects and HTTP responses.

reveal.text: Do not choose Global Accelerator when the core requirement is edge caching of objects and HTTP responses.

prompts.label: 🎯 EXAM CLUE
prompts.placeholder: Cache content at edge locations points to __________; static anycast IPs for a global TCP service point to Global Accelerator.

reveal.text: Cache content at edge locations points to CloudFront; static anycast IPs for a global TCP service point to Global Accelerator.

source_refs.title: Determine high-performing and/or scalable network architectures — official exam guide
CloudFront vs Global Accelerator — AWS documentation

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: ALB provides __________ HTTP routing, NLB provides high-performance Layer 4 TCP and UDP load balancing, and GWLB integrates fleets of network virtual appliances.

reveal.text: ALB provides Layer 7 HTTP routing, NLB provides high-performance Layer 4 TCP and UDP load balancing, and GWLB integrates fleets of network virtual appliances.

prompts.label: ⏱️ WHEN?
prompts.placeholder: Use ALB for host or path routing, NLB for transport-level performance and static-IP style requirements, and GWLB for transparent inspection __________.

reveal.text: Use ALB for host or path routing, NLB for transport-level performance and static-IP style requirements, and GWLB for transparent inspection appliances.

prompts.label: 🚫 NOT THIS
prompts.placeholder: Do not use an __________ when the workload requires UDP forwarding.

reveal.text: Do not use an ALB when the workload requires UDP forwarding.

prompts.label: 🎯 EXAM CLUE
prompts.placeholder: HTTP path routing points to __________; UDP or extreme Layer 4 performance points to NLB; appliance insertion points to GWLB.

reveal.text: HTTP path routing points to ALB; UDP or extreme Layer 4 performance points to NLB; appliance insertion points to GWLB.

source_refs.title: Determine high-performing and/or scalable network architectures — official exam guide
ALB, NLB, and GWLB — AWS documentation

nodes.title: Direct Connect, VPN, Transit Gateway, and PrivateLink

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: Direct Connect provides __________, Site-to-Site VPN provides encrypted IPsec connectivity, Transit Gateway acts as a network transit hub, and PrivateLink exposes services privately through endpoints.

reveal.text: Direct Connect provides dedicated connectivity, Site-to-Site VPN provides encrypted IPsec connectivity, Transit Gateway acts as a network transit hub, and PrivateLink exposes services privately through endpoints.

prompts.label: ⏱️ WHEN?
prompts.placeholder: Select based on bandwidth consistency, encryption requirements, __________, and whether the goal is network connectivity or private service access.

reveal.text: Select based on bandwidth consistency, encryption requirements, topology scale, and whether the goal is network connectivity or private service access.

prompts.label: 🚫 NOT THIS
prompts.placeholder: Do not use VPC peering as a transitive hub for a large many-VPC topology because peering relationships are __________.

reveal.text: Do not use VPC peering as a transitive hub for a large many-VPC topology because peering relationships are not transitive.

prompts.label: 🎯 EXAM CLUE
prompts.placeholder: Many VPCs plus on-premises networks needing hub-and-spoke connectivity points to __________.

reveal.text: Many VPCs plus on-premises networks needing hub-and-spoke connectivity points to Transit Gateway.

source_refs.title: Determine high-performing and/or scalable network architectures — official exam guide
Direct Connect, VPN, Transit Gateway, and PrivateLink — AWS documentation

modules.title: Determine high-performing data ingestion and transformation solutions

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: Kinesis Data Streams provides real-time streaming with application-controlled consumers, Data Firehose delivers __________ to destinations with minimal management, and Amazon MSK provides managed Apache Kafka.

reveal.text: Kinesis Data Streams provides real-time streaming with application-controlled consumers, Data Firehose delivers streaming data to destinations with minimal management, and Amazon MSK provides managed Apache Kafka.

prompts.label: ⏱️ WHEN?
prompts.placeholder: Choose Kinesis for custom stream processing, Firehose for __________, and MSK when Kafka compatibility is a core requirement.

reveal.text: Choose Kinesis for custom stream processing, Firehose for managed delivery, and MSK when Kafka compatibility is a core requirement.

prompts.label: 🚫 NOT THIS
prompts.placeholder: Do not choose Firehose when applications need __________ shard-level consumer control and custom stream retention semantics.

reveal.text: Do not choose Firehose when applications need fine-grained shard-level consumer control and custom stream retention semantics.

prompts.label: 🎯 EXAM CLUE
prompts.placeholder: Kafka protocol compatibility points to MSK; managed delivery to S3 or Redshift points to Data __________.

reveal.text: Kafka protocol compatibility points to MSK; managed delivery to S3 or Redshift points to Data Firehose.

source_refs.title: Determine high-performing data ingestion and transformation solutions — official exam guide
Kinesis, Data Firehose, and MSK — AWS documentation

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: AWS Glue provides managed data integration and ETL, EMR runs big-data frameworks, Athena runs serverless SQL on data in S3, and Redshift provides a __________.

reveal.text: AWS Glue provides managed data integration and ETL, EMR runs big-data frameworks, Athena runs serverless SQL on data in S3, and Redshift provides a managed data warehouse.

prompts.label: ⏱️ WHEN?
prompts.placeholder: Choose according to whether the workload needs ETL, framework-based processing, __________ over S3, or warehouse-style analytics.

reveal.text: Choose according to whether the workload needs ETL, framework-based processing, ad hoc SQL over S3, or warehouse-style analytics.

prompts.label: 🚫 NOT THIS
prompts.placeholder: Do not provision a __________ cluster only to run occasional serverless SQL queries directly against S3 data.

reveal.text: Do not provision a Redshift cluster only to run occasional serverless SQL queries directly against S3 data.

prompts.label: 🎯 EXAM CLUE
prompts.placeholder: Ad hoc SQL over S3 points to __________; managed Spark or Hadoop points to EMR; ETL catalog and jobs point to Glue.

reveal.text: Ad hoc SQL over S3 points to Athena; managed Spark or Hadoop points to EMR; ETL catalog and jobs point to Glue.

source_refs.title: Determine high-performing data ingestion and transformation solutions — official exam guide
Glue, EMR, Athena, and Redshift — AWS documentation

nodes.title: DataSync, Storage Gateway, and Snow Family

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: DataSync moves data __________ between storage systems, Storage Gateway supports ongoing hybrid access patterns, and Snow Family devices move or process data where network transfer is impractical.

reveal.text: DataSync moves data online between storage systems, Storage Gateway supports ongoing hybrid access patterns, and Snow Family devices move or process data where network transfer is impractical.

prompts.label: ⏱️ WHEN?
prompts.placeholder: Use network transfer when __________ and time allow it; use Snow devices when the dataset or site constraints make network transfer too slow.

reveal.text: Use network transfer when bandwidth and time allow it; use Snow devices when the dataset or site constraints make network transfer too slow.

prompts.label: 🚫 NOT THIS
prompts.placeholder: Do not ship a Snow device for a __________ online migration that DataSync can finish comfortably within the migration window.

reveal.text: Do not ship a Snow device for a small online migration that DataSync can finish comfortably within the migration window.

prompts.label: 🎯 EXAM CLUE
prompts.placeholder: Petabyte-scale migration from a bandwidth-constrained site points toward __________ Family.

reveal.text: Petabyte-scale migration from a bandwidth-constrained site points toward Snow Family.

source_refs.title: Determine high-performing data ingestion and transformation solutions — official exam guide
DataSync, Storage Gateway, and Snow Family — AWS documentation
